clue.text: With money in the bag, acknowledgements of debt are wide-ranging

indicators.note: the word in tells us the money is placed inside the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch
P stands for penny or pence, a unit of money
an IOU ('I owe you') is a written acknowledgement of a debt, here plural

explanation.surface: A bag stuffed with cash, and the IOUs owed are sprawling too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' reads as where the money is kept, but it is simply a synonym supplying letters that hold the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spacious is roomy and broad in scope, covering a lot of ground.

clue.text: The South houses people — people from the North

parts.note: cots are small cottages, humble houses
men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: The southern half of the country is home to folk who come from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a verb meaning contains, but it is the noun, giving COTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland lies in the north of Britain, so its natives are northerners.

clue.text: Sale doing badly, close

indicators.note: something done badly is botched or jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sale is going poorly and is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SALE DOING into the answer; 'close' is the adjective, near, not the verb to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside or next to, that is, near at hand.

clue.text: Some disdain dialect in this country

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people look down on the local dialect of their nation.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation, so it is an example of a country; the definition reads 'in this country', locating the hidden name.

clue.text: All the same, it's clothing of a kind

explanation.surface: Everything matches, since it is a particular sort of dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means identical throughout, and is also the standard outfit worn by soldiers, pupils or staff.

clue.text: Make a great show of putting political leader in nick

indicators.note: the word in shows the leader's letter goes inside the nick

parts.note: a slash is a cut or nick

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grand display of jailing a party chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like British slang for prison, but here it means a cut, SLASH; P goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash out or make a splash is to do something showy and attention-grabbing.

clue.text: Awfully inert characters put inside — in prison — get fit

indicators.note: put inside says one set of letters is placed within another

parts.note: pent means shut in or confined, as in a prison

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done terribly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lazy inmates locked up in jail should get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'in prison' look like an aside about inmates, but it is the word meaning confined, which 'put inside' opens up around the jumble 'Awfully' makes of 'inert'; 'characters' just means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent is relevant and apposite, fitting the matter in hand.

clue.text: A ship with quarters for animals

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
E and S are two compass quarters, east and south

explanation.surface: A vessel fitted with stalls for carrying livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' sounds like accommodation, but it means compass points, here E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are donkeys, a kind of beast.

clue.text: A supplier of basic knitwear

parts.note: read as a trade description: someone who sells stockings and socks, the most elementary knitted garments

explanation.definitionFit: A hosier is a trader in hose, that is stockings and socks, which are knitted goods.

clue.text: Given support, didn't quit

explanation.surface: Propped up, they refused to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop, so a stayed mast is supported; stayed also means remained rather than left.

clue.text: There's nothing, absolutely nothing, like an egg

parts.note: O, the round zero, stands for nothing
a void is complete emptiness

explanation.surface: Total emptiness resembles the shape of an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, from the Latin ovum.

clue.text: Concerns trendy testers-out

parts.note: something in is fashionable

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Worries about fashionable product testers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is attached to 'testers' to look like a phrasal noun, but it rearranges TESTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerns are matters one cares about or businesses one has a stake in.

clue.text: Evidence a Conservative is a subscriber

parts.note: a sign is evidence or an indication
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Proof that a Conservative has signed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subscriber' is used in its old sense of one who writes their name beneath a document.
explanation.definitionFit: One who subscribes to a document puts their name under it, i.e. signs it.

clue.text: Children can be a problem!

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that kids can be trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring in legal language, and also a point in dispute or difficulty.

clue.text: "A dwarfish whole, its body brevity and wit its soul." (Coleridge)

definitions.text: "A dwarfish whole, its body brevity and wit its soul." (Coleridge)

parts.words: A dwarfish whole, its body brevity and wit its soul." (Coleridge)
parts.note: Coleridge's own two-line verse defining a short, pointed witty saying

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Coleridge's famous couplet of definition: 'What is an Epigram? A dwarfish whole...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's couplet describes a brief witty poem or saying, short in body and clever in spirit.

clue.text: Virtuous rogue? This must be erroneous!

indicators.note: an erroneous arrangement is a wrong one, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Calling a rascal virtuous? That has to be a mistake!
explanation.definitionFit: Righteous means morally upright and good.

clue.text: Get a draught from a medico in French religious house

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medico
en is the French word for in
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Receive a dose from a doctor at a church in France.
explanation.walkthrough: A drench is a dose of medicine poured down an animal's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A drench is a large liquid dose of medicine given to livestock.

clue.text: Honoured companion, like the Venus de Milo but without the grace

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
the famous Greek statue of Venus has lost both its arms

explanation.surface: A distinguished companion resembling the armless statue, but lacking her elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmless means lacking appeal or attractiveness.

clue.text: Stall on a municipal thoroughfare? That's typical

parts.note: a stand is a market stall
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A market stall on a town street is a common sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or usual, the regular kind.

clue.text: A church official apparently on edge

explanation.surface: A nervous churchwarden.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: a VERGE-ER would be someone on the verge, or edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger looks after a church interior; the second sense jokingly treats the word as 'one on the verge'.

clue.text: He works constructively, topping fellow!

parts.note: read as a builder whose job is putting the top on a building, rather than praise for a great chap

explanation.definitionFit: A roofer is the tradesman who builds the covering on top of a house.

clue.text: Being late with brochure, pull out

parts.note: ex means former, so late in the sense of no longer in office
a tract is a pamphlet or brochure

explanation.surface: The leaflet is overdue, so withdraw it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like overdue, but means former, EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw or remove something out.

clue.text: The pledge is sincere

explanation.surface: The promise is genuinely meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest is money paid as a deposit to secure a deal, and also means serious and heartfelt.

clue.text: Rare fright about cold

indicators.note: about says the first part goes round the second

parts.note: a scare is a fright
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An unusual shock involving a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means in short supply, seldom found.

clue.text: Expertise, or just trickery?

explanation.surface: Is it skill, or merely deceit?
explanation.definitionFit: Craft means skill, as in a trade, and also cunning or guile.

clue.text: Athenian garret

explanation.surface: An attic room in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes things from Attica, the region of Athens; it is also a room just under the roof.

clue.text: Ladies who look forward to a good row!

definitions.text: Ladies who look forward to a good row!

parts.words: Ladies who look forward to a good row!
parts.note: seems to describe women relishing a quarrel, but row means pulling a boat, and rowers sit facing backwards

explanation.definitionFit: Women who row boats are rowers, and they enjoy a good outing on the water.

clue.text: Composed, though put down

explanation.surface: Calm, even though deflated.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose music or verse is to write it, and to put words down on paper is also to write.

clue.text: Draw back, or deer etc will scatter

indicators.note: letters that scatter are dispersed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Retreat, or the deer and other beasts will run off.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrocede is to move backwards or recede.

clue.text: Love having quiet period for music

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
P stands for piano, the musical instruction for quiet
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Romance with a calm interlude makes for a good tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music, so a form of musical composition.

clue.text: A tax cut

explanation.surface: A reduction in duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a duty levied on goods; to excise is to cut out surgically.

clue.text: On reflection, sweets make one put weight on

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: desserts are sweet courses, called sweets in Britain

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, puddings make a person gain pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put weight on' looks like gaining weight, but means emphasised.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a word or point is to give it extra force.
